arxiv-2105-07936.title: A Two-Sided Matching Model for Data Stream Processing in the Cloud – Fog Continuum
arxiv-2105-07936.creator: Narges Mehran, Dragi Kimovski, Radu Prodan, Institute of Information Technology, Alpen-Adria-Universität Klagenfurt, Austria Email: {name}.{surname}@aau.at
arxiv-2105-07936.description: Abstract Latency-sensitive and bandwidth-intensive stream processing applications are dominant traffic generators over the Internet network. A stream consists of a continuous sequence of data elements, which require processing in nearly real-time. To improve communication latency and reduce the network congestion, Fog computing complements the Cloud services by moving the computation towards the edge of the network.

arxiv-2110-06623.title: SSSNET: Semi-Supervised Signed Network Clustering
arxiv-2110-06623.creator: Yixuan He, Gesine Reinert, Songchao Wang, Mihai Cucuringu
arxiv-2110-06623.description: Abstract Node embeddings are a powerful tool in the analysis of networks; yet, their full potential for the important task of node clustering has not been fully exploited. In particular, most state-of-the-art methods generating node embeddings of signed networks focus on link sign prediction, and those that pertain to node clustering are usually not graph neural network (GNN) methods.

arxiv-2111-05601.title: Subelliptic Operators on Weighted Folland-Stein Spaces
arxiv-2111-05601.creator: Hung-Lin Chiu
arxiv-2111-05601.description: Abstract . In this paper, we show that the sub-Laplacian of an asymptotically flat pseudo-hermitian manifold defined on a suitable weighted Folland-Stein spaces is an isomorphism. Similarly in dimension 5 5 a certain Dirac-type operator is shown to be an isomorphism, which is used to resolve the CR positive mass problem 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification.

arxiv-2203-01333.title: Liouvillian skin effect in an exactly solvable model
arxiv-2203-01333.creator: Fan Yang, Qing-Dong Jiang, Emil J. Bergholtz
arxiv-2203-01333.description: Abstract The interplay between dissipation, topology and sensitivity to boundary conditions has recently attracted tremendous amounts of attention at the level of effective non-Hermitian descriptions. Here we exactly solve a quantum mechanical Lindblad master equation describing a dissipative topological Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain of fermions for both open boundary condition (OBC) and periodic boundary condition (PBC).

arxiv-2207-10937.title: Physics-informed convolutional neural network with bicubic spline interpolation for sound field estimation
arxiv-2207-10937.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . A sound field estimation method based on a physics-informed convolutional neural network (PICNN) using spline interpolation is proposed. Most of the sound field estimation methods are based on wavefunction expansion, making the estimated function satisfy the Helmholtz equation. However, these methods rely only on physical properties; thus, they suffer from a significant deterioration of accuracy when the number of measurements is small. Recent learning-based methods based on neural networks have advantages in estimating from sparse measurements when training data are available.

arxiv-2306-11754.title: Pre-Pruning and Gradient-Dropping Improve Differentially Private Image Classification
arxiv-2306-11754.creator: Kamil Adamczewski, Yingchen He, Mijung Park
arxiv-2306-11754.description: Abstract Scalability is a significant challenge when it comes to applying differential privacy to training deep neural networks. The commonly used DP-SGD algorithm struggles to maintain a high level of privacy protection while achieving high accuracy on even moderately sized models.

arxiv-2307-11311.title: Entropy and fluctuation relations in isotropic turbulence
arxiv-2307-11311.creator: H. Yao 1, T.A. Zaki 1, C. Meneveau 1
arxiv-2307-11311.description: Abstract Based on a generalized local Kolmogorov-Hill equation expressing the evolution of kinetic energy integrated over spheres of size ℓ \ell in the inertial range of fluid turbulence, we examine a possible definition of entropy and entropy generation for turbulence.

arxiv-2401-12049.title: Copacabana: A Probabilistic Membership Assignment Method for Galaxy Clusters 2024 Copacabana: A Probabilistic Membership Assignment Method for Galaxy Clusters – A

arxiv-2401-12049.description: Abstract Cosmological analyses using galaxy clusters in optical/NIR photometric surveys require robust characterization of their galaxy content. Precisely determining which galaxies belong to a cluster is crucial. In this paper, we present the CO lor P robabilistic A ssignment of C lusters A nd BA yesia N A nalysis (Copacabana) algorithm.

arxiv-2501-04609.title: Incoherent horizontal emittance growth due to the interplay of beam-beam and longitudinal wakefield in crab-waist colliders
arxiv-2501-04609.creator: Peter Kicsiny, Demin Zhou, Xavier Buffat, Tatiana Pieloni, Mike Seidel
arxiv-2501-04609.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate quadrupolar sychrobetatron resonances caused by beam-beam collisions and their interplay with longitudinal wakefields in the context of crab-waist colliders. We present a comprehensive theoretical review of the established theory of sychrobetatron resonances and extend the formalism to explore horizontal sychrobetatron resonances specific to crab-waist colliders.

arxiv-2508-05867.title: The Memory Wars: AI Memory, Network Effects, and the Geopolitics of Cognitive Sovereignty
arxiv-2508-05867.creator: Mario Brcic
arxiv-2508-05867.description: Abstract The advent of continuously learning Artificial Intelligence (AI) assistants marks a paradigm shift from episodic interactions to persistent, memory-driven relationships. This paper introduces the concept of ”Cognitive Sovereignty” , the ability of individuals, groups, and nations to maintain autonomous thought and preserve identity in the age of powerful AI systems, especially those that hold their deep personal memory.

arxiv-2510-25765.title: FreeArt3D: Training-Free Articulated Object Generation using 3D Diffusion 1209 Conference: SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 Conference Papers; December 15–18, 2025; Hong Kong, Hong Kong SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 Conference Papers (SA Conference Papers ’25), December 15–18, 2025, Hong Kong, Hong Kong DOI: 10.1145/3757377
arxiv-2510-25765.creator: Chuhao Chen, Isabella Liu, Xinyue Wei, Hao Su, Minghua Liu
arxiv-2510-25765.description: Abstract . Articulated 3D objects are central to many applications in robotics, AR/VR, and animation. Recent approaches to modeling such objects either rely on optimization-based reconstruction pipelines that require dense-view supervision or on feed-forward generative models that produce coarse geometric approximations and often overlook surface texture.

arxiv-2511-04480.title: Upper critical in-plane magnetic field in quasi-2D layered superconductors
arxiv-2511-04480.creator: Huiyang Ma, Dmitry V. Chichinadze, Cyprian Lewandowski
arxiv-2511-04480.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Huiyang Ma, Dmitry V. Chichinadze, Cyprian Lewandowski. The study of the interplay of applied external magnetic field and superconductivity has been invigorated by recent works on Bernal bilayer and rhombohedral multilayer graphene. These studies, with and without proximitized spin-orbit coupling, have opened up a new frontier in the exploration of unconventional superconductors as they offer a unique platform to investigate superconductivity with high degree of in-plane magnetic field resilience and even magnetic field-induced superconductivity.

pmc-10694332.title: Exploring LIPIDs for their potential to improves bioavailability of lipophilic drugs candidates: A review
pmc-10694332.creator: Preeti, Sharda Sambhakar, Renu Saharan, Sonia Narwal, Rohit Malik, Vinod Gahlot, Asaad Khalid, Asim Najmi, Khalid Zoghebi, Maryam A. Halawi, Mohammed Albratty, Syam Mohan
pmc-10694332.description: This review aims to provide a thorough examination of the benefits, challenges, and advancements in utilizing lipids for more effective drug delivery, ultimately contributing to the development of innovative approaches in pharmaceutical science. Lipophilic drugs, characterized by low aqueous solubility, present a formidable challenge in achieving effective delivery and absorption within the human body.

pmc-11425115.title: Investigating the electrochemical properties of poly(vinylidene fluoride)/polyaniline blends doped with lithium-based salt
pmc-11425115.creator: Mahdi Kargar-Esfandabadi, Marzieh Golshan, Hossein Roghani-Mamaqani, Mehdi Salami-Kalajahi
pmc-11425115.description: Conductive polymers have attracted much attention in various applications, owing to their excellent chemical, thermal, and oxidative stability. However, they have low dielectric constant, which limits their performance in electrochemical devices. To overcome this drawback, blending with other polymers helps improving their electrochemical properties.

pmc-11579153.title: Transverse and oblique course of the vertebral artery over the medullospinal junction
pmc-11579153.creator: Ana-Maria Davidoiu, Mugurel Constantin Rusu, Corneliu Toader, Petrinel Mugurel Rădoi
pmc-11579153.description: PurposeThe vertebral artery (VA) pierces the dura mater and continues with the intradural V4 segment. Once entered into the dura mater, the VA ascends from the infero-lateral to the antero-superior side of the medulla. Scarce reports of VAs compressing the medullospinal junction (MSJ) are available.

pmc-12630985.title: Implementation of real-time optimization control to reduce environmental impact in laser diode assisted sustainable leather cutting
pmc-12630985.creator: Vasanth Swaminathan, M Mohamed Rabik, Rowida Meligy, Ismail Chekalil
pmc-12630985.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Semiconductor laser diode machining has emerged as a disruptive solution improving precision and efficiency in leather cutting making it an indispensable technology in industries such as automotive and aerospace. This study investigates the improvement of Normalized Performance Index (NPI) through the application of Extremum Seeking Control (ESC) to optimize the laser diode cutting process focusing on minimizing carbonization and kerf width while maximizing material removal rate (MRR) to improve the overall process efficiency.

pmc-12788466.title: Radiomics and Machine Learning in Early Detection of Oral Potentially Malignant Disorders
pmc-12788466.creator: Ashwini Dhopte, Vikas Singh, J Sophia J. Priya, Sumit Bhatt, Prasad C. Ingale, Hiroj Bagde
pmc-12788466.description: Oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) are a diverse group of conditions that carry a risk of transformation into oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Early detection is vital to improving prognosis and survival. Recent advancements in radiomics and machine learning (ML) have shown promise in enhancing the diagnostic accuracy and early detection of OPMDs.

pmc-12996254.title: School-based mindfulness education and children’s emotion regulation: the mediating role of executive function
pmc-12996254.creator: Xuhong Wang, Xuefei Dong
pmc-12996254.description: BackgroundSchool-based mindfulness education has been increasingly implemented to support children’s socio-emotional development; however, the cognitive mechanisms underlying its effects on emotion regulation remain insufficiently clarified. This study examined whether mindfulness-based education improves children’s emotion regulation and whether executive function mediates this association.

pmc-13046653.title: Role of Complement Component 9 in Bone Health: Causal Evidence in Humans and Mechanistic Studies in Mice
pmc-13046653.creator: Claes Ohlsson, Anna E. Törnqvist, Karin H. Nilsson, Maria Nethander, Jianyao Wu, Lei Li, Antti Koskela, Sofia Movérare-Skrtic
pmc-13046653.description: Complement component 9 (C9) is the main pore-forming protein of the terminal membrane attack complex (MAC) in the complement system. The MAC forms a lytic pore in the membrane of target cells and is a key effector of the innate immune system.
